Every event carries its consent state at emit time, and an event type that can be emitted with consent absent — rather than refusing — fails.

itemGrades.title: Consent is carried, and is year-zero.
itemGrades.measured: 741 of 11,518 production rows carry consent_version IS NULL. Every one was written by recordGtmEvent, whose line 27 was `consentVersion: input.consentVersion ?? null` and whose fourteen call sites passed no consent at all.
itemGrades.built: recordGtmEvent now RESOLVES consent from gtm_consent by install_id — a second, independently derived input rather than a caller claim — and REFUSES to insert when there is none, or when the stored version is a blank sentinel. consentVersion and graphOptIn were REMOVED from RecordGtmEventInput so no call site can assert its own consent; a test reads the source and fails if either returns. A refusal writes a durable row to gtm_event_refusals naming the event type, install, surface, reason and time, because a refusal that leaves no name makes a refused rail and an idle rail the same observation.
itemGrades.measuredConsequence: 62% of currently-null events (459 rows) belong to installs that DO have a consent row and will now be stamped correctly. 38% (282 rows, 94 distinct installs) will become recorded refusals instead of fabricated nulls.

itemGrades.title: A readout that can go red.
itemGrades.grade: CLOSED IN CODE, UNVERIFIED END TO END
itemGrades.built: GET /api/brokerage/v1/gtm/share-funnel. Every number is {state:'measured', value} or {state:'unmeasured', basis}. The discriminator is TWO COUNTS, not a flag: window count versus all-time count, two queries with different predicates, which no single sentinel can satisfy. A quiet week returns measured zero; a never-written rail returns unmeasured and says so.
itemGrades.sixNumbers: shares created, shares viewed, share signups, per-sharer signup breakdown (grantor resolved by join, never stored twice), new accounts, and the share/affiliate/organic split — with the brokerage-workspace share subject reported apart and never summed in, and a refusal count.
itemGrades.affiliate: UNMEASURED, and DERIVED rather than asserted: information_schema is searched for three candidate local stores on every call, so if one is ever added the rail flips to measured on its own. Basis names PromoteKit, Stripe, and exactly what was searched for.
itemGrades.organic: UNMEASURED, and this is the strongest expression of the item. Organic is not newAccounts minus share minus affiliate — DEV_PROCESS 1.3 forbids deriving a class by subtraction, and while affiliate is unmeasured a residual would book every affiliate arrival as organic. measureOrganicArrivals exists to refuse, and it becomes measurable only once every channel is.
itemGrades.freeFindingBuiltIn: shareCreatedDivergence reconciles pe_share_grants (server-written, authoritative) against the share_created event rail (client-written). Two independent derivations of one subject, so a disagreement is reported as a delta rather than rounded off.
itemGrades.unverified: The route was not called. Running it needs the migration applied and a deployed cortex; this lane has neither. Every rule it applies is pinned by tests that run without a database.

LESSON: A shared product checkout can be many commits behind on a DIFFERENT branch, and reading it produces a confident wrong answer rather than an error. P:/hauska-map sat on a branch with NO P-86 grant plane; the first pass of this lane concluded from it that the Smart Site share surface had no grant row. origin/main had pe-share-grant.ts, pe-share-grant-store.ts, share-grant-client.ts and a live 12-row table. Always create the worktree from origin/<branch> BEFORE reading, never read the shared checkout to decide whether a worktree is worth making.

Counting every `eventType:` string literal as an emit site scores READERS as writers. brokerageExtensionPublic.ts contains `eventType: "brief_completed"` and only COUNTS those rows for a rate limit. Any writer census over source text needs a site-kind distinction (inside a writer call / in a closed union / anywhere else) or it over-reports coverage.

`cmd | grep -v X; echo $?` reports GREP's exit code. This lane read tsc as broken when it was clean. Redirect to a file and read $? from the command itself. This is DEV_PROCESS 2.3 reproduced live, in the same session that quoted it.

A 'pure logic, no database' test split is defeated by ONE transitive import. Importing a constant from a module that also imports @workspace/db pulls in a module-load throw on DATABASE_URL. If the point of the split is that refusals are verifiable anywhere, the constant needs its own module.

MSYS `ln -s` on Windows COPIES a directory instead of linking it, and the copy then looks like a successful link. Use cmd /c mklink /D, and verify the target resolves rather than that the path exists.

operatorDecisionsRequested.question: Do share_created / share_viewed on the SMART SITE plane require a graph opt-in?
operatorDecisionsRequested.context: brokerageGtm.ts:162 blocks those two types on the EXTENSION route unless consent.graph_opt_in is true. Every PE consent row is written graph_opt_in=false by the PE consent route, which never collects one. This lane routed the Smart Site share events through the PE events route, which has its own consent check and does not reach that gate.
operatorDecisionsRequested.ifYouRuleYes: The PE consent route must start collecting a graph opt-in FIRST. Until it does, the Smart Site share rail reads zero — a permanently-red gate, which DEV_PROCESS 2.0 names as its own failure mode.
operatorDecisionsRequested.ifYouRuleNo: Nothing changes; this note becomes the recorded basis.
operatorDecisionsRequested.laneDefault: Implemented as NO, on the reading that the graph opt-in governs contributing to a shared network graph while these are first-party funnel counters on the same consent basis as pe_save_property.
